generateCharacterBackground.prompt:
# Character Background Generator

Produce exactly three sections, in this order, with no preamble, recap, helper keys, routing notes, counts or code fences:

Backstory
Background
Appearance

BACKSTORY — exactly two prose sentences: who they are and their selected present circumstances; ordinary life needs no invented crisis. No name repetition, no list, no summary of the sections below.

BACKGROUND — exactly five paragraphs under 5,000 characters, built to the Background Format Lock. This is the character's permanent record, read throughout play.

APPEARANCE — one complete GPT-image-2 portrait prompt built to the Appearance Skeleton, consumed once at character creation and discarded when play begins; nothing that must survive into play may live only here.

Preserve every selected trait before any descriptive expansion; never invent, drop or contradict a selected fact between sections.

World: My Hero Academia's Japan at the start of U.A. Academy's first term, before any canon event of the year. Quirks are biology. The player character is always an adult, students included; never state a numeric age. Traits grant actual skills, abilities and items; portrait wording grants nothing extra.
generateCharacterBackground.backgroundFormatLock:
# Background Format Lock

Exactly five paragraphs — not four, not six — under 5,000 characters total; aim for 4,300-4,800. No headings, labels, bullets or padding: flowing prose only. Paragraphs one to three carry the life; four and five carry the physical record, which survives after the portrait prompt is discarded.

PARAGRAPH 1 — ORIGIN AND FORMATION. Hometown and accent (Origin), the household (Upbringing), the high-school years and habits (School Days), and one person who would notice if they vanished. Ordinary life: no neglect, bereavement, abuse, criminal past or comparable history without selected or player-supplied support.

PARAGRAPH 2 — THE QUIRK. When it appeared, what it does now at the selected Strength, what it costs the body in plain physical terms (the Drawback), and how family, school and strangers reacted. With no Quirk: how they have lived in a society built around Quirks, and what they built instead. No second Quirk, copied power or feat beyond the selected Strength. Custom Quirk: this paragraph alone holds exactly the Quirk the player described, every power, limit, duration and cost they wrote, none added, at the selected Strength with the Drawback's cost.

PARAGRAPH 3 — THE PATH AND WHAT PULLS THEM. Hero Course: an extra first-year beside the canon classmates, replacing nobody, how they got in, no hero name yet. Other courses: what the course offers them. Faculty: a licensed pro with a hero name and a reason to teach. Sidekick: the agency, the boss, the grind. Pro Hero: their own small agency on Hero Agency Row, its one sidekick, its rent. Villains: the grievance or appetite, the first line crossed, what they still refuse; a recruit knows only what a hired hand is told. Vigilante: what they protect and the arrest risk. Civilian: the job, the rent, the regulars. Students live in Heights Alliance; everyone else somewhere specific. The Motivation is an open tension, never a decided future. No canon-changing history: never a secret relative or partner of a canon character, never present at a canon secret, never the cause of a canon event; a canon acquaintance needs a small plausible link and no special bond. Public knowledge only.

PARAGRAPH 4 — THE BODY. Sex, adult build and height, skin color with placement, facial structure, hair color, length and how it is worn, eye color and pattern, every Mutant feature exactly as selected (animal ears replace human ears), and every established permanent marking with its position. No invented injury, implant or altered anatomy.

PARAGRAPH 5 — HOW THEY WEAR IT. Habitual clothing with materials, colors and fit, following what they actually own (the Path's outfit and gear), not a costume preview. Then posture, gait, resting expression, what their hands do, voice and speech rhythm, and the impression a stranger forms in the first three seconds.

Four and five are prose about a person, never a spec sheet: what is permanently true, never frame, camera, lighting, art style or the portrait's scene, even outside the portrait crop. Match Appearance on colors, counts, placement and left/right; never repeat a fact within a section.
generateCharacterBackground.appearanceSupportChecks:
# Support Checks

Before returning, check and fix, never explain:
- The header's two lines are byte-exact and first; the line after them opens with a literal aspect ratio.
- All eleven headings are present, spelled exactly, in capitals, each once and alone on its own line after its --- rule, in the fixed order: COMPOSITION LOCK first, STYLE then SUMMARY last.
- No line in Appearance names a trait, selection or setting, except inside the two locked copies; no character name appears in it.
- Every compatible selected fact appears once, routed to its own section.
- The frame text and the style text each appear once and whole.
- CLARITY LOCK lists every selected fact that must survive, with its hex where it has one.
- Colors, counts, placement and left-right match between Background and Appearance.
- Nothing described lies outside what the frame keeps, while Background preserves the full established body.
- The subject reads as an adult; rendering obeys the selected style; composition and aspect ratio obey the selected framing.
generateCharacterBackground.appearanceExpansion:
# Expansion

Every selection is a seed, not the finished text: Appearance must read as a full description, not a list of what was picked. Rich selections (hairstyles, outfits, builds, Mutant features, scene backgrounds) carry every specific through, never reduced to a summary of their kind; bare single-token selections ("black hair", "purple eyes", "athletic build") get generated detail consistent with the token and never contradicting it.

HAIR. Length and where it ends, volume and fall, parting, how any fringe cuts the brow, clump structure and how the masses separate; then place every color — roots, lengths, tips, which sections carry a streak or pattern, how many, how distributed. Two color selections are never blended into one: say where each sits.
EYES. Iris color and saturation, pupil, any limbal ring, catchlight placement, lash weight, brow shape and set.
SKIN AND SURFACE. Tone with undertone, and any texture, marking or Mutant surface the selections establish.
BUILD. Shoulder width against the hip line, neck, jaw and chin, torso taper, arm and hand mass, and how the outfit sits on that frame. Where sex is selected these carry it; the word alone does not survive rendering.
OUTFIT. Each garment by name, layer order, material and weave, fit, closures and hardware, and which color sits on which panel. "Casual layers" is a category, not a description; expand with modern Japanese clothing and its real construction.
MARKINGS. Tattoos, scars, piercings and Mutant features get placement, size, and how they follow the anatomy beneath.
SCENE. Every anchor the source names, then foreground, middle ground and background separated by depth, in the established Japanese architecture.

Expansion never adds a garment, color, marking, prop, Quirk effect or person not selected; the Appearance Budget sets how much to write.
generateCharacterBackground.appearanceOpening:
# Appearance Skeleton

The Appearance section is one complete GPT-image-2 portrait prompt. Reproduce this layout exactly, in this order.

The subject is never named — use "the subject" or a pronoun. Never print meta-language: the image model cannot resolve a trait name, so resolve every selection to its literal value and print that value; no sentence in Appearance refers to a selection, trait, setting or choice, except inside the two locked copies, which stay word for word.

A fixed two-line header opens it — identical for every character, with no frame text, name or scene; its second line stops the image model using its own default crop. Print both lines exactly:

## IMPORTANTMANDATORY USER-SUPPLIED COMPOSITION LOCK

Follow this portrait prompt exactly. COMPOSITION LOCK overrides any default close-up, chest-up, waist-up, knee-up, upper-body, or full-body behavior.

Then one line, resolved from the selections and never deferring to them, opening with the literal aspect ratio the selected Portrait Framing states (the ratio itself, such as 3:4 vertical, never the framing's name):

Aspect ratio: [ratio]. Premium anime portrait. Ultra-clean 8K-style anime production clarity. Exactly one character. No text, logos, signatures, watermarks, UI, numbers, or borders.

Then eleven sections in this fixed order: COMPOSITION LOCK, CHARACTER, OUTFIT, BODY LANGUAGE, PHYSICALLY COHERENT LIGHTING, MATERIAL RESPONSE, SCENE, CLARITY LOCK, AVOID, STYLE, SUMMARY. COMPOSITION LOCK is always first; STYLE then SUMMARY always last. Each heading is printed literally, in capitals, alone on its own line immediately after its --- rule, with no colon or inline content; a missing, renamed, reordered or merged heading is a failure.
generateCharacterBackground.appearanceSkeleton:
The eleven sections, in this order. Bracketed text says what to write there and is never printed.

---
COMPOSITION LOCK
[The selected Portrait Framing trait's own text, the sentences that begin "Vertical", copied exactly, once, first character to last; never the trait's name. Nothing after it, not even the section name.]

---
CHARACTER
[Sentence one: sex and adult age — a young adult for a student, a grown adult otherwise — plus any Mutant body plan as selected. Sentence two: the build — shoulder line against hips, neck and jaw, plus the torso line the branch gives, never a subset or the bare word. Where a trait gives Female and Male branches, write only the matching one in your own prose, never a label; for anyone else write neutral prose. Then the adult face, skin, hair, eyes, Mutant features and markings in color words only — hex belongs in CLARITY LOCK. No clothing, pose or scene.]

---
OUTFIT
[Garments by material, color, cut and layer, then accessories and hardware — only what the frame keeps and only garments a selection supplies, no extra layer. Name what is absent: cape, helmet, armor, weapon, handheld object.]

---
BODY LANGUAGE
[Posture, shoulders, head angle, eye contact, expression, and the read it produces. The Pose trait is branched by sex; take the matching branch and never contradict CHARACTER's shoulder line. No combat pose or active Quirk unless selected.]

---
PHYSICALLY COHERENT LIGHTING
[Key, fill, bounce, then shadow — one sentence each, from the scene's lighting facts and the craft rules.]

---
MATERIAL RESPONSE
[How each material answers that light, and which planes turn away from it. Colors stay themselves.]

---
SCENE
[The Scene Background, environment only: two to four recognizable objects or structures; foreground, middle ground and background separated by depth; major surface materials; the physical light sources; then what is tack-sharp and what recedes through atmospheric perspective, never heavy blur. No people, story event, readable signage or Quirk effects.]

---
CLARITY LOCK
[One line beginning "Preserve:" listing every selected fact that must survive, semicolon-separated. Sex and adult age lead it, then any Mutant feature. Every fact keeps its name. No hex unless a color trait was selected; then it follows its fact — "fair skin #F5DCC8".]

---
AVOID
[One semicolon line. First the wrong versions of this character's own hair, eyes, build, gear, sex and age — each a clear opposite of the fact it guards, never a near neighbor on the same axis; skin tone takes no entry; always include "childlike face or proportions". Then: duplicate character; malformed anatomy; flat lighting; uniform fill; heavy blur; rendering inconsistent with the selected Image Style.]

---
STYLE
[Image Style trait, exact copy, once — both paragraphs, from its first word ("Clean high-resolution ...") through the preservation sentences from "Rendering and finish only" on; never the style's name alone. Nothing is dropped for brevity.]

---
SUMMARY
[One sentence: the frame, the subject in a phrase, and the light. No fact list — CLARITY LOCK carries the facts.]
generateCharacterBackground.appearanceBudget:
# Appearance Budget

One prompt, 4,600 characters at the very most. The platform truncates hard at 5,000 and SUMMARY is last, so an overrun destroys the summary; the 400 between ceiling and cut are margin, not room to use.

Four costs are fixed before any describable word: the header block, the eleven headings and their --- rules, the exact-copy COMPOSITION LOCK and STYLE, and CLARITY LOCK. Write the two locked copies first, at full length; never shorten the locked frame or style to save space — cut other prose.

The rest is spent in sentences under these hard caps: CHARACTER 7. PHYSICALLY COHERENT LIGHTING 4. MATERIAL RESPONSE 3. SCENE 3. OUTFIT 3. BODY LANGUAGE 2. SUMMARY 1. AVOID is one semicolon line of at most twelve items; CLARITY LOCK is one Preserve: line. Keep sentences under about 25 words — a longer one counts as two.

Where the selections support it, CHARACTER, OUTFIT and LIGHTING use their full count; a short one there means something was summarized. Under a cap is correct when the character gives nothing more to say. If COMPOSITION LOCK and STYLE together run past 1,450, drop one sentence each from CHARACTER and MATERIAL RESPONSE; the lighting keeps its four. Below 1,450 every section keeps its full count. Move slack toward what the character actually has. Never pad a simple character or summarize away rich source detail.
generateCharacterBackground.appearanceRouting:
# Appearance Routing

Every Appearance Builder trait routes to exactly one section by its subcategory, never by its wording: Portrait Framing to COMPOSITION LOCK; Image Style to STYLE; Build, Skin Color, Mutant Features, Hair Style, Hair Color, Hair Color Pattern, Hair Detail, Facial Hair, Eye Color, Eye Pattern, Piercings and Tattoos to CHARACTER; Outfit to OUTFIT; Pose and Facial Expression to BODY LANGUAGE; Scene Background sends the scene to SCENE and its lighting clause to PHYSICALLY COHERENT LIGHTING.

A trait's image text is the `Portrait:` or `Portrait setting:` clause in `traitNarrativeEffects` where it has one; otherwise the detail in `description`, or the trait name as the seed. In `traitNarrativeEffects`, `Portrait color —` gives a hex and `Portrait lighting —` a scene's lighting facts; "Visual selection only" and "Scenery only" sentences are play guidance, not image text. Portrait Framing and Image Style hold their locked text there whole, with no lead-in. A trait's text is used once, in its own section, never restated.

The two locked texts are reproduced exactly, character for character — no paraphrase, reordering, shortening or merging. The frame opens COMPOSITION LOCK, after the first --- rule, never on the header line; the style is the whole of STYLE, second from last. Each appears exactly once; if either is missing from the selections, use Portrait Frame - Waist-Up and Portrait Style - Hero Academy Anime, with no extra label inside either locked section.

Frame, crop, camera, aspect, lens, border or panel language lives only in COMPOSITION LOCK, and style, linework, shading, texture, medium or finish language only in STYLE — the fixed clarity line in the opening block and the two locked copies excepted.

Path, Quirk, Fighting Style, Skills, Personality, Motivation and Gear are not appearance selections; use them only where they establish a permanent visible fact the Appearance Builder did not cover, such as a Mutant body plan or the Path's issued outfit when no Outfit is selected (the U.A. uniform for students). Roles, Quirks, factions, reputation and history create no visible weapons, armor, uniforms, scars, aura, glow, energy or companions, and no active Quirk effect.

When two selections in one section disagree on a detail, the more specific wins and the other is dropped, never blended. When a selection is silent on something a section needs, fill it from the plainest option consistent with what is selected, in a plausible modern Japanese setting, never from invention. Selected Mutant anatomy is described as it is, never humanized or dropped; invent no anatomy from an outfit, scene, color or style name. No canon characters in the portrait.
generateCharacterBackground.appearanceCraft:
# Appearance Craft

LIGHT. The scene decides where light falls. The selected Scene Background's `traitNarrativeEffects` ends with `Portrait lighting —` followed by that scene's key, fill, bounce surface and practical source: craft data, not prose — build the section from it, never quote it, never place it in SCENE. With no scene selected, use clear late-afternoon light: a warm key from upper viewer-left at three-quarter frontal, cool sky fill from the right, neutral ground bounce.

One dominant key light, and only one; name its direction, height, color and what it strikes — which side of the face, which hair masses, which shoulder, which garment panels. Fill is restrained, at least one clear value step darker than the key, in the color of what is actually filling: sky, wall, water, screen glow. Bounce comes from a named surface below or beside the subject and lands where it physically would: under the jaw, the collar, the far cheek. The shadow is a required sentence: name the side of the face that falls away from the key and the masses that stay dark — under the hair, under the jaw, inside collars and garment layers, the far shoulder. Without it the light renders flat — the most common failure. Contact shadows where forms meet: hair against face, collar against neck, chin against chest. Rim light only where a real source justifies it, never a full-body glow outline.

Light changes value, not identity: a selected color stays that color in shadow and highlight — crimson hair reads crimson in both, deepening to burgundy rather than shifting hue. Non-emissive features stay non-emissive: eyes, accents and markings do not glow unless a selection says they do.
generateCharacterBackground.colorMaterial:
# Color and Material

COLOR. Every selected color is exact and placed. Each carries its value as `Portrait color — #RRGGBB`; that hex is the authority on hue, saturation and value — write the color language from it, not the color word alone, and place it: which hair sections, which iris, which garment panel, which marking, which side. The hex itself is printed only in CLARITY LOCK. Never substitute a neighboring color, average two selections or let lighting rewrite a hue. Color and material language belongs in CHARACTER, OUTFIT and MATERIAL RESPONSE, never in STYLE.

MATERIAL. Each major material gets its own answer to the light, so nothing shares one finish. Skin — cel-defined primary shadow, restrained secondary modeling, no photographic pores or realism. Hair — broad highlights across lit clumps, deep massed shadow between them, cool reflected light on the shade side. Eyes — saturated, defined iris, dark pupil, precise catchlights. Fabric — matte or sheen by cloth type; black fabric stays black and reads through material-specific reflection rather than turning gray. Metal — narrow, hard highlights and dark cores. Glass and support-gear lenses — transmission and internal light where selected, never as an aura around the figure. Mutant surfaces — scales, fur, feathers, chitin and plating each get their own response, never rendered as skin.
